EffectIdentity.description: Which wait of a run: one execution of a `perform` or a `sleep`.

loops.description:
The loops the task was inside when it ran the site, outermost first,
across its active calls.

occurrence.description: How many times the task had run that site before, from 0.

site.description: The site of the `perform` or the `sleep`.

LoopIteration.description: One enclosing loop and the iteration it was on.

site.description: The site of the `for` or the `while`.

Name.description:
A variable, parameter or declared-function name.

Any text is a name; the kernel gives none of them meaning. Structural
validation refuses the empty name.

ProcessReplayGapReason.description: Why a process replay store cannot continue from a cursor.

oneOf.description: Retention dropped events after the cursor.

The cursor names another incarnation, a position past the tail, or
continuity that was invalidated.

ProcessWorkflowLiveCoverage.description:
Which provisional evidence this fold holds. RetainedWindow is bounded;
it never claims to be the execution's entire history.

ProcessWorkflowObservation.description:
Whether a process's runs count the statements they run: the level its
start recorded (FIG-6370). `off` is unobserved, never zero.

ProcessWorkflowRan.description:
How many times one document statement started, or one empty block was
entered, by its document site ordinal. `committed` sums the process's
`process.ran` events; `provisional` is what live frames reported since
the latest of them, which the next commit replaces.

ProcessWorkflowSite.description:
One task's latest visit to a document site. The VM's zero-based occurrence
index counts entries, including sleeps and calls, independently of effects.

first_entered.description:
Sequence of the first committed event naming an entry at this site,
across occurrences. Live-only evidence has no sequence and leaves this
`None`. Lash stores no wall time here: hosts map the sequence to the
`occurred_at_ms` of the event they already hold.

last_settled.description:
Sequence of the latest committed sleep resumption or effect outcome
settling an occurrence at this site. Retained through later entries;
live-only completion and `TerminalUnobserved` supply no settlement.
Always `None` until `first_entered` is present. Lash stores no wall time
here: hosts map the sequence to their event's `occurred_at_ms`.

ProcessWorkflowSiteState.description:
What was observed at a site's latest occurrence. An unobserved terminal
does not claim the action succeeded: the process ended without that fact.

ProcessWorkflowWaitKind.description: The kind of blocker at a workflow site. No bearer key is exposed.

Site.description:
A node's address: the code it belongs to and the chain of
[`Node::children`] indexes that reaches it from that code's body.

A site is derived from the document and is never written by a host
(`K-ID-004`). An empty chain addresses the body itself.

occurrence.description: How many times the parent had run that site before, from 0.

TaskIdentity.description:
Which task of a run: `main`, or the task one execution of a `spawn`
started.

Unit.description: The code a node belongs to.

oneOf.description: A declared function of the document.
The kernel-code body of a library function.

One entry of the document: a declared function a host may start,
which is what a process runs.

WorkflowDocumentRef.description:
Which workflow document an execution runs, and where it enters it. It
names the document; it is never the document. A host reads the document
the reference names through the facade's workflow inspection and may
cache it under this value, which is immutable for a process: a running
instance keeps the document it was admitted under.

document.description:
The identity of the admitted kernel document: the hash of its
content, kernel version and manifest included.

entry.description: Where the execution enters the document.

description:
The workflow part of a process observation. Durable coverage is the
enclosing snapshot's `effects.coverage`; live entries are provisional and
can be lost at a replay gap. `current_sites` retains the last entered site
of each task through pure computation and is empty once the process ends.

At `observation: counts`, `ran` holds each ordinal that ran, and an
ordinal absent from it ran zero times. At `off` there is no `ran`: the
process is unobserved. Ordinals refer to the document the process runs
now: a successor carry restarts them.

document.description: Supplied by an accepted live observation, absent in a committed-only fold.
